title: Chunky fingerless mitts
subtitle: Quick fingerless mitts in chunky wool, knitted flat and seamed.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts in chunky-weight wool, knitted flat in 2x2 rib and seamed up the side with a small gap for the thumb. A very quick knit for beginners. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Flat-knitted ribbed wrist warmers seamed up the side with a thumb gap are documented in Weldon's Practical Knitter from the 1880s onward. The chunky adaptation uses the same construction.

knitting.gaugeText: 14 sts × 18 rows = 10 x 10 cm in 2x2 rib slightly stretched on 6 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm. Length 20 cm on all sizes.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of seaming two pieces of knitting together invisibly from the right side. The yarn is threaded through the bars between the edge stitches on each piece alternately, drawing the two edges together without a visible ridge.

content.text: Fingerless mitts in chunky-weight wool, knitted flat in 2x2 rib and seamed up the side with a thumb gap, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
This is a very quick knit: each mitt takes about 30 minutes at chunky gauge. The flat construction means straight needles work fine, and the seam is closed with
mattress stitch
. The thumb gap is left unworked in the seam. Budget about 80 g (120 m / 130 yards) of chunky-weight yarn per pair.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 80 g (about 120 m / 130 yards) of chunky-weight wool or wool blend

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 6 mm (UK 4 / US 10) straight or circular needles

content.text: Gauge

14 stitches and 18 rows to 10 cm in 2x2 rib slightly stretched on 6 mm needles. Check your gauge by working a small swatch and measuring it with the rib pulled out to the width it will sit on a hand. If your gauge is 15 stitches per 10 cm, your size M mitt will be about 1 cm narrower at the palm.
Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 24 (28, 32) stitches. For 32 stitches at 6 mm needles, pull off about 28 cm of tail before starting.
Mitt body
Row 1 (RS): *k2, p2*; repeat to end. Row 2 (WS): *p2, k2*; repeat to end. Repeat rows 1 and 2 until the piece measures 20 cm from the cast-on edge. Bind off in pattern.
Stitch count check: you should have 24 (28, 32) stitches throughout. 2x2 rib does not increase or decrease.
Seaming
Fold the piece in half lengthwise with right sides facing out. Pin the cast-on and bind-off edges together. The seam runs along the side edge.

Using mattress stitch: seam from the cast-on edge upward for 6 (7, 7) cm (the cuff section), then leave a 3.5 (4, 4) cm gap for the thumb, then seam the remaining 10.5 (9, 9) cm up to the bind-off edge.
Mirror your second mitt

Work the second mitt identically but reverse the seaming direction: seam from the bind-off edge downward for 10.5 (9, 9) cm, leave the thumb gap, seam the remaining 6 (7, 7) cm. The thumb gap will then sit on the opposite side when worn.
Common faults

Both thumb gaps on the same side: the seaming start point was not reversed on the second mitt. Measure where the gap sits on the first mitt (6 cm from the cast-on edge), then start the second mitt seam from the bind-off end.
Seam too tight, mitt rolls inward: the mattress stitch yarn was pulled too firmly. Work mattress stitch with the seam yarn at the same tension as the knitted fabric.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Steam the seam gently with a damp cloth if needed to flatten it.
Care
Hand wash in cool water with a wool-safe detergent. Lay flat to dry.
What to try next
The in-the-round version of the same mitt avoids the seam entirely and teaches the magic-loop technique. Chunky weight at 6 mm needles on magic loop is a practical first round project.
